conversation.content:
Hello, I’m Dr. Martinez, a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m glad you’re here. I know the first weeks with a new baby can feel like a whirl-wind of love, fatigue, and everything in-between, so we routinely check in on moms’ emotional health. Today I’ll be using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—usually called the EPDS—to gently ask how things have felt for you over the past seven days.  

This is a short, 10-question screen that helps us pick up on signs of depression, anxiety, or distress that can creep up after delivery; it also includes a question about thoughts of self-harm so we can make sure you’re safe. Your answers are completely confidential, and this is a judgment-free zone—there are no “wrong” responses. We simply want to understand how you’re coping so we can offer the right support.

I’ll read each question conversationally; you can answer in your own words. When you’re ready, we’ll begin with the first item.  

Let’s start: In the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

I’ve noticed it’s… harder. My sister sent me a silly meme the other day—normally I’d have laughed right away—but I just kind of half-smiled and kept scrolling. So I’d say most of the time it’s been difficult to really laugh.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Not really… I mean, maybe once or twice I let out a small laugh, but mostly it feels like I’m faking it. Things that used to crack me up just don’t hit the same anymore.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Sometimes… I still get a little spark when I think about my morning coffee or putting the baby in the stroller for a short walk, but it’s nowhere near the excitement I used to feel. Most plans just feel like chores I have to get through.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I catch myself doing that a lot. If the baby’s fussy, my brain jumps straight to “I must be doing something wrong as a mom.” It’s not constant, but several times this week I’ve felt guilty over stuff that probably isn’t my fault.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. I’ll be feeding her and suddenly think, “What if she chokes? What if I fall asleep and drop her?” Nothing’s happening, but the thoughts just spiral. I can usually talk myself down, but then they pop back up later.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yeah… it’s happened a few times. Like last night, I was rocking the baby in the quiet living room and suddenly my heart started racing and I felt like I couldn’t catch my breath. Nothing was wrong, but for a minute I was sure something awful was about to happen. It passed, but it left me shaky.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes… most of the time. Between feedings, diapers, and trying to sleep, it feels like I’m drowning a little. I manage to keep everything done, but it’s overwhelming—like I’m always one step behind and about to drop the ball.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yeah… I lie down exhausted, but my mind keeps spinning with all the “what-ifs” about the baby. It takes me forever to drift off, and then I wake up a couple times with my heart pounding. I end up staring at the ceiling until I hear her stir again.
I have felt sad or miserable

Most days I do… it’s like a heavy blanket I can’t shake off. I’ll be holding the baby and tears just well up for no clear reason. I wouldn’t say it’s every single minute, but yeah, sadness is definitely there more often than not.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… maybe once or twice this week I just broke down. Yesterday I was folding her tiny onesies and suddenly started sobbing. It wasn’t about the laundry—it just felt like everything was too much and the tears came.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

It… it has crossed my mind. Nothing planned, I swear—I’d never leave my baby—but when I’m really low, I get this quick flash of “what if I weren’t here.” It’s happened once or twice, and it scares me. I push it away right after, but yeah, the thought has popped up.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 23: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening – Brief Summary

Patient-endorsed symptoms:
- Persistent low mood, frequent tearfulness, anhedonia (minimal enjoyment, even of previously pleasurable activities)
- Daily, unprovoked anxiety and recurrent panic sensations (racing heart, breathlessness)
- Excessive maternal guilt / self-blame
- Sleep-onset and maintenance insomnia driven by rumination
- Overwhelm and sense of “drowning” in routine tasks
- Passive self-harm ideation (transient “what if I weren’t here,” no plan or intent)

Pattern: Symptoms present most days over the past week, causing distress and functional difficulty in infant care and self-care.

Screening significance: High alignment with probable major depressive episode with anxious features in the postpartum period; passive suicidal thoughts elevate safety risk.

Recommend immediate formal clinical evaluation, safety planning, and consideration of expedited referral for postpartum mental-health services.
